title: Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions, Part II: critical Hecke values
summary: Construct equivariant coherent Eisenstein–Kronecker classes and their critical evaluations over totally imaginary fields admitting a lifted CM type. Compare them with explicitly normalized analytic currents and orbit Eisenstein series, prove critical-value integrality and period algebraicity, and construct ordinary p-adic ray-class interpolation. Generic Poincaré, CM, cohomology and measure theories are imported. The independent nonordinary CM direction has its own split proposal.
readme: The reader specifies nine construction-ordered layers, all targets, definition APIs and tests, source locators, exact supplier contracts and three mathematical proof obligations.

stages.title: Critical types and CM coefficient lines
stages.description: Fix the lifted CM type of a totally imaginary field containing its maximal CM subfield, and distinguish the value index α from the derivative index a=α−1. Specify the based CM abelian datum over an arithmetic model and its two cotangent actions. Identify exactly the critical invariant divided-power coefficient lines. Generic diagonalizable-group weight decompositions, CM Serre tensors and Hodge eigenspaces are imported; only their critical-value specialization is owned here. Targets: Lifted CM types and critical coefficient indices; CM abelian data with bases and torsion; Critical coefficient invariants.

stages.title: Residues and equivariant Eisenstein–Kronecker classes
stages.description: Specify trace-zero functions on finite étale torsion, the equivariant support-cohomology residue calculation and the completed inverse-limit comparison. Define the unique Eisenstein–Kronecker class with prescribed trace-zero residue and its invariant derivatives. Prove independence and functoriality using the existing completed Poincaré bundle. The construction retains the actual finite-level equivariant cohomology and its transition maps rather than treating a pro-sheaf as an ordinary coherent sheaf. Targets: Trace-zero functions on étale torsion; Equivariant residue and inverse-limit comparison; Equivariant coherent Eisenstein–Kronecker class; Flat derivatives of the coherent class.

stages.title: Critical evaluation and integral refinement
stages.description: Evaluate at torsion by the imported splitting principle and group moment maps, then cap the critical group-cohomology component with the oriented free-unit fundamental cycle. Establish finite-index scaling, the refined evaluation that does not invert Nf, and its comparison with the unrefined value. Compare the residue class with the imported logarithm/polylogarithm construction. For unit groups with torsion, normalized evaluation is integral only where the torsion order is invertible or a separate divisibility theorem applies. Targets: Torsion specialization and group-cohomology moments; Orientation-normalized critical Eisenstein classes; Change of unit subgroup with its normalization; Refined evaluation without inverting the conductor norm; Comparison of refined and unrefined evaluations; Comparison with the de Rham polylogarithm.

stages.title: Analytic representatives and current normalization
stages.description: Construct the CM Borel differential complex using imported forms and the bundle-valued current resolution. Define the generalized lattice Eisenstein–Kronecker functions, their gamma-completed Mellin continuation and their phase-sensitive functional equation. Normalize the current by the corrected contraction recurrence and verify its differential equation with the specified residue. Distinguish the poles of K from those of π^(−s)Γ(s)K; keep the inverse covolume factor and the negative trace-Fourier convention. Targets: Unit Borel model and relative Dolbeault complex; Relative currents and residue-normalized integration; Generalized Eisenstein–Kronecker series; Poisson continuation with completed residues; Residue-normalized Eisenstein–Kronecker current; The current realizes the coherent class.

stages.title: Orbit sums and explicit critical classes
stages.description: Define convergent unit-orbit Eisenstein series and their continuation by integration over the logarithmic unit torus. Prove the gamma-factor fibre integral with a fixed orientation and measure. Identify the analytically represented critical class, including the corrected weight-dependent sign and dual-period conversion. The full algebraic-residue/current/orientation comparison is an explicit theorem obligation, so the interpolation proof cannot silently drop its sign. Targets: Eisenstein series over unit orbits; Fibre integration of Kronecker series; Explicit critical class in analytic and algebraic bases.

stages.title: Periods and integral critical Hecke values
stages.description: Attach periods and ideal structures to the Serre tensor datum and define the exact factorial and two-period normalizer. Identify ray-partial Hecke values with orbit Eisenstein sums; prove residue-value integrality, torsion distribution and full critical-value integrality with its auxiliary-ideal factor. Deduce algebraicity, the generalized Shimura formula and the weak Deligne period relation. The latter permits a zero L-value. Full-unit integral normalization is a separate divisibility obligation at nonunit torsion indices. Targets: Ideal structures and compatible complex periods; Critical-value normalization; Partial Hecke L-functions as unit-orbit series; Integrality of normalized Eisenstein sums; Torsion distribution and the smoothing identity; Integral differences of partial critical values; Regularized integrality and algebraicity; Katz–Shimura algebraicity for totally imaginary extensions; Deligne period comparison modulo algebraic units.

stages.title: Ordinary levels and p-adic theta coordinates
stages.description: Define p-ordinarity for the lifted type without requiring L itself to be a CM field. Specify connected multiplicative levels, paired étale isogenies, canonical differentials and unit p-adic periods. Construct the CM Eisenstein theta class using the imported integral Poincaré trivialization, and identify invariant differential moments with its algebraic critical evaluations. The finite-free multivariable Amice transform is an input from the measure roadmap. Targets: Ordinary lifted types and CM level structures; Canonical differentials and p-adic periods; The p-adic theta function of a residue class; Canonical formal derivatives and embedding monomials.

stages.title: Eisenstein measures and partial Fourier moments
stages.description: Construct the bounded Eisenstein measure, retaining the extra Σ-period factor caused by the determinant line. Prove translation through the étale ordinary isogeny, define the normalized one-direction Weil-pairing Fourier transform, and compute locally constant twists of all critical moments. The transform divides by p^(dn), its character sign is negative, and its individual coefficients need not be integral even when the original theta measure is integral. Targets: The CM Eisenstein measure and its moments; p-power translation with Weil-pairing weights; Normalized partial Fourier transform; Locally constant twists of Eisenstein moments.

stages.title: Ray-class interpolation and bounded desmoothing
stages.description: Define Katz’s local factor with its conductor decomposition and the correct extension at trivial Σ-components. Specify auxiliary-ideal Dirac smoothing atoms and construct smoothed ray-class measures using the tame-congruence unit closure. Prove bounded removal of the smoothing factors, then the fully normalized interpolation formula for critical characters with both complete p-Euler products. Sign compatibility, integral unit-index descent and uniform measure-algebra divisibility are explicit proof obligations; the CM-field case compares with the existing Katz measure. Targets: Katz’s local factor for a lifted ordinary type; Auxiliary-ideal smoothing measures; Smoothed ray-class measures from the CM Eisenstein measure; Bounded removal of auxiliary ideals; Critical Hecke-value interpolation over totally imaginary fields.
